test_title: PYST 28: SSC GD Constable 2025 - General Knowledge (Held On: 18 Feb, 2025 - Shift 1)
subject: gk
question: Which of the following statements about the National Population Policy 2000 is incorrect?

options.text: Providing free and compulsory schooling up to the age of 14 years
Achieve universal immunization of children against all vaccines
Reducing infant mortality rate to below 15 per 1000 live births

solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **National Population Policy (NPP) 2000** was introduced to address the unmet needs of contraception, healthcare infrastructure, and health personnel.
 
• The policy aims to achieve a stable population by **2045**, consistent with sustainable economic growth, social development, and environmental protection.
 
• One of the goals is to reduce **infant mortality rate (IMR)** to below 30 per 1000 live births by 2010, not 15 as mentioned in Option 4.
 
• It promotes **universal immunization** for children, free and compulsory education for children up to age 14, and delayed marriage for girls to reduce fertility rates.
 
• The policy also emphasizes increasing access to reproductive healthcare services and creating awareness about family planning.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Infant Mortality Rate (IMR):**

 
 
• IMR refers to the number of infant deaths (under 1 year of age) per 1000 live births in a given year.
 
• According to the NPP 2000, the goal was to reduce IMR to less than 30 by 2010.
 
• Achieving a low IMR is crucial for improving the overall health of a population.
 
 
 
• **Universal Immunization Programme (UIP):**
 
 
• Launched in 1985, UIP is one of the largest health programs globally, targeting vaccine-preventable diseases.
 
• It aims to immunize children against diseases such as polio, tuberculosis, measles, and diphtheria.
 
• UIP aligns with the NPP 2000 objective of universal child vaccination.
 
 
 
• **Free and Compulsory Education:**
 
 
• The policy emphasizes free and compulsory education for children up to 14 years of age as a means to empower them and reduce fertility rates.
 
• This is in line with the Right to Education (RTE) Act, 2009.
 
 
 
• **Delayed Marriage for Girls:**
 
 
• NPP 2000 promotes raising the marriage age for girls to 18 or higher to improve maternal and child health.
 
• Delayed marriage helps reduce adolescent pregnancies and ensures better health outcomes for mothers and children.
 
 
 
• **Goals of NPP 2000:**
 
 
• Achieve replacement-level fertility (Total Fertility Rate of 2.1) by 2010.
 
• Reduce maternal mortality ratio (MMR) to below 100 per 100,000 live births by 2010.
 
• Promote contraception and access to reproductive health services for all.
